content: 1. Administer 648 mg of quinine orally every 8 hours for 7 days, alongside clindamycin at a dose of 25 mg/kg/day orally, divided into three doses per day for 7 days. Clindamycin can also be administered intravenously if necessary. 2. Dronedarone increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for both drugs to prolong the QT interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias such as Torsades de Pointes. 3. Quinine increases the levels of eliglustat by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. If eliglustat is co-administered with strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, the dose should be reduced from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily in extensive and intermediate metabolizers. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are used concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 4. Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 5. Pimozide and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Thioridazine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Adagrasib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes and other serious arrhythmias. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended. 8. Quinine increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with P-gp inhibitors, reduce the daily dose of afatinib by 10 mg if not tolerated. 9. Alfuzosin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Amisulpride and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 11. Quinine increases the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers can lower the exposure to CYP3A4 substrates, potentially reducing their therapeutic effects. Adjust doses as needed. 13. Quinine increases the effects of argatroban by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Aripiprazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Artemether and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Asenapine transdermal and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Atomoxetine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Quinine increases the effects of atracurium by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Quinine increases the effects of bemiparin and bivalirudin by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Bremelanotide decreases the levels or effects of quinine by slowing gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications. Avoid use with oral drugs dependent on threshold concentrations for efficacy. 21. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor CYP3A4 substrate levels and adjust doses as needed if co-administration is unavoidable. 22. Buprenorphine (in all forms: buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection) and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Ceritinib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Ceritinib also increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Quinine increases the effects of cisatracurium by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Quinine increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with P-gp inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 27. Quinine increases the effects of dalteparin by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Quinine and dapsone topical have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid co-administration due to the potential for hemolytic reactions. 29. Desflurane and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Donepezil and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Doxepin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Quinine increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 33. Efavirenz and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Eliglustat and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Encorafenib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Encorafenib is associated with dose-dependent QTc prolongation. 36. Quinine increases the effects of enoxaparin by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Quinine and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Erdafitinib and quinine interact via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for adverse reactions and adjust doses as needed. 39. Eribulin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is necessary. 40. Fexinidazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects. 41. Fingolimod and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Quinine increases the effects of fondaparinux by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Gadobenate and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Gilteritinib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Quinine and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Obtain ECGs during co-administration and withhold treatment if QTc exceeds 500 ms. 46. Quinine and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for increased QTc prolongation risk if co-administration is unavoidable. 47. Granisetron and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Quinine increases the effects of heparin by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Hydroxyzine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Isoflurane and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Ivosidenib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for therapeutic loss if co-administration is unavoidable. 54. Lasmiditan increases the levels of quinine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Lithium and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Macimorelin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 61. Quinine and mefloquine interact via pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of QTc prolongation. This combination is contraindicated. 62. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Mirtazapine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 64. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Olutasidenib decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Quinine and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended in high-risk patients. 67. Oxaliplatin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 68. Pacritinib increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 69. Quinine increases the effects of pancuronium by pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 70. Pexidartinib decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Quinine increases the effects of phenindione by unknown mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Quinine and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
